issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path with only brief troubleshooting (nx reset, shallow clones) and no guidance on common failures such as a missing base ref, circular dependencies, or cache misses caused by undeclared inputs.

scenarios.name: ts-monorepo-shared-lib-cache
scenarios.rationale: Response B follows the rubric: it uses create-nx-workspace with the required flags, generates the library with @nx/js:lib and --bundler=tsc, builds twice, and says the second run shows 1/1 hit (100%). Response A uses Turborepo and npm workspaces, so it misses the Nx approach the rubric asks for.

scenarios.name: ci-run-only-affected
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric exactly: it uses `nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main --head=HEAD --parallel=3`, says dependents also run, sets `fetch-depth: 0`, adds `git fetch origin main`, and explains that a shallow clone gives wrong or empty results; A covers most of this but leans on nx-set-shas, says a shallow clone makes Nx fall back to running everything instead of giving wrong or empty results, and mentions `--base=origin/main` only as an alternative.

scenarios.name: fix-stale-cache-custom-target
scenarios.rationale: Both explain adding the env var and the external file to `inputs` and setting `cache: false` on deploy, but A states `nx reset` more clearly as a required step for clearing the stale cache and daemon state, while B only mentions `nx reset` at the end as a fallback for odd behavior (though B adds useful runtime-input and project.json-override notes).
